title: First exponents make every restricted coefficient determinant nonzero
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $L$ a field, $m,n,s\in\mathbf N$, $\alpha:\operatorname{Fin}(s)\to\mathbf N^n$ an ordered vertex family for $D$ [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division], and $c_{i\gamma}\in A$. Let $e:A\to L$ and $T:A\to L[[W_1,\ldots,W_m]]$ be ring maps with $\operatorname{constantCoeff}(T(r))=e(r)$ for every $r\in A$. Form $f_i$ and $M_{q,t}$ by [def-trf-coefficient-division-data]. Assume the first nonzero coefficient of $f_i$ in total-degree lexicographic order, with $W$ before $Z$, occurs at $(0,\alpha_i)$. Then $e(\det M_{q,t})\ne0$ for every prefix degree $q\in\mathbf N$ and every $t\in\mathbf N$. No monotonicity, geometry or stabilization bound is assumed.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Lemma 7.7 pp.263--264, Theorem 8.1 pp.273--275, and completion of Theorem 9.6 p.282. BM read online at https://mahalex.net/teaching/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 is the route reference.

proof.text: Assign each generator column (i,beta) its exponent alpha_i+beta. The least dividing vertex is its inverse; the remainder columns account exactly for exponents outside the diagram. This is a degree-preserving bijection. Restriction to essential variables preserves the vertices and their degrees.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Lemma 7.7 pp.263--264, Theorem 8.1 pp.273--275, and completion of Theorem 9.6 p.282. BM read online at https://mahalex.net/teaching/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 is the route reference.

proof.text: Extending an essential-variable monomial by zero first to Z and then to (W,Z) preserves comparisons between equal-degree exponents. The first-exponent hypothesis therefore gives zero entries before the assigned exponent in each column and the nonzero diagonal ev(c_i,alpha_i). Monomial multiplication preserves this order; remainder columns have diagonal 1.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Lemma 7.7 pp.263--264, Theorem 8.1 pp.273--275, and completion of Theorem 9.6 p.282. BM read online at https://mahalex.net/teaching/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 is the route reference.

proof.text: Evaluate the matrix through ev and order its rows and columns by assigned exponent. The permutation formula for a triangular determinant gives the product of its nonzero diagonal entries. Coefficient maps commute with determinants. Thus the evaluated determinant is nonzero, including the empty determinant.
